messages.hasTypeAndArg: `defineEmits` has both a type-only emit and an argument.
messages.definedInBoth: Custom events are defined in both `defineEmits` and `export default {}`.

cases.code:
<script lang="ts" setup>
        /* ✓ GOOD */
        defineEmits({ notify: null })
      </script>

<script lang="ts">
        const def = { notify: null }
      </script>
      <script lang="ts" setup>
        /* ✓ GOOD */
        defineEmits(def)
      </script>

<script lang="ts" setup>
        defineEmits({
          notify (payload) {
            return typeof payload === 'string'
          }
        })
      </script>

<script setup lang="ts">
      import type { PropType } from 'vue';

      type X = string;

      const props = defineProps({
        myProp: Array as PropType<string[]>,
      });

      const emit = defineEmits({
        myProp: (x: X) => true,
      });
      </script>

<script setup lang="ts">
      import type { PropType } from 'vue';

      const strList = ['a', 'b', 'c']
      const str = 'abc'

      const props = defineProps({
        myProp: Array as PropType<typeof strList>,
      });

      const emit = defineEmits({
        myProp: (x: typeof str) => true,
      });
      </script>

<script lang="ts" setup>
      import { propsDef, emitsDef } from './defs';

      defineProps(propsDef);
      defineEmits(emitsDef);
      </script>

<script lang="ts" setup>
        /* ✗ BAD */
        const def = { notify: null }
        defineEmits(def)
      </script>

<script setup lang="ts">
        /* ✗ BAD */
        defineEmits<(e: 'notify')=>void>({ submit: null })
      </script>
